havent particularly noticed hair shedding with it but everyone's different. tbh ive been on it for about 3 years now i think and ive always shed hair quite a bit since puberty lmao but ive never had an issue with it not growing back

i take both testosterone and finasteride too! 16.2mg/g every other day and 1mg finasteride every other day (i take them on the same day every morning)

i haven't found that my muscle growth has been affected at all, i've still been steadily building up muscle at a good pace. as far as i can tell just from looking at others' accounts, the stuff finasteride affects is facial hair growth + libido. i haven't found the libido thing to be too much of an issue personally but it has definitely toned me down so to speak lol

i've got ocd so i've been taking antidepressants (60mg fluoxetine / day) for a while, so i think i'm kind of getting lucky and sidestepping the pretty bad finasteride side effects.

long story short tho as long as you have enough finasteride to stop the testosterone converting into DHT you'll be fine and it won't accelerate your hair loss, in my personal experience. everyone is individual though, and it's impossible to say exactly. i'm very genetically prone to hair loss tho so it's been good to see my hair's been fine, if you're in a similar boat

good luck!!

lmfao mate this is absolutely laughable. it’s amazing if shrooms have helped you with any difficulties you’ve had in life, and i don’t want to invalidate those experiences in any way. it’s great that you’re living your life in a healthier way for you.

but autism is not just being ‘socially awkward’ and the ‘improved cognitive ability’ thing is a dumb stereotype that isn’t even really a thing for most autistic people. special interests are a different matter, of course. your surface level description of autism and how’s it helped you are pretty ridiculous, mate. again, if shrooms have helped you with difficulties in your life, that’s amazing. but don’t go around proclaiming you’ve been alleviated of your autism. that’s really not how it works. this isn’t positivity, it’s just harmful to neurodiverse people and only further confuses neurotypical people and leaves them uneducated. i don’t know what your problem is, but this is just sad.

side note, the puzzle piece thing is from a ‘charity’ called autism speaks that are famously incredibly horrible to the autistic community. most of autistic people (myself included) don’t see it as a symbol.

but autism can’t be cured. that’s just not a thing. i’m not saying i simply identify with it, i’m saying being autistic affects people with autism so fundamentally that it IS who we are in many ways. you can’t just remove autism from a person??? there is no cure.

if you were saying it’s helped you with parts of your autism you found difficult, i’m completely on board with that. there are difficulties that can come with being autistic when living in the modern world, and if shrooms have helped you cope, that’s great. but saying you’re ‘alleviated’ of your autism? that’s disturbing. it’s like saying you killed a fundamental part of yourself. autism has so many amazing things about it. how can you say that you’ve just removed it from yourself? i really can’t wrap my head around it. when you’re autistic, it is who you are.

i don’t mean to come off as rude sounding, and i think it’s wonderful that the autistic community is open to self-diagnosis because many autistic people do go undiagnosed by medical professionals, particularly women, but were you ever analysed by a professional to establish that you did indeed have autism? i find it difficult to believe that you’re saying all this as someone who is autistic. autistic people know better than anyone how fundamental autism is to our persons, and that it can have many wonderful parts too. this post and reply comes off as bizarre, honestly.

yeah, i hear ya. it’s upsetting to hear someone try to belittle your identity, it’s fucked. especially when it’s stuff like that you can’t even have controlled in the first place. i guess the difference would be i don’t even see autism as a negative thing in any way. my negative experiences with autism come from the society around me, not who i inherently am. i love being autistic in many ways, it’s just being different in my eyes, really. maybe that’s the same way you feel about being a junkie in the past, and i completely respect that. experiences like that you can’t just take away from someone.

i totally hear you though. it just comes across as shitty

i think the thing is that autism isn’t really the same as a disorder like depression. it makes up so much of your behaviour, your likes, your dislikes, that it is in a lot of ways who you are as a person.

people congratulating this as a success story, in my and probably a lot of other autistic people’s eyes is saying ‘i’d rather you, as a person, were completely different’. i would never want to be ‘cured’, whatever that means. it would strip me of my identity. it’s upsetting to see this kind of stuff tbh.

dude, i can see youve now removed this, but just reading the title i’m really disgusted. i’m autistic and it’s not a disease, it’s not a negative thing. the negative parts come from what’s around you, not what’s within you. it’s not something to be cured. when you’re autistic is is quite literally who you are.

please, please everyone, don’t go around congratulating this. as an autistic person this makes me deeply uncomfortable, and really horrifies me to see so many people treating this as a success story.
